title: Derived evaluation factors through the normalized constant diagonal
statement:
Let $C_n$ be arbitrary commutative rings with inverse transition homomorphisms. On small pro-etale scheme sites use $\mathscr S_T$, $\mathcal T_T(C_n)$, exact evaluation $e_{n,T}$, the exact constant-diagram functor $\Delta_T$, and specified ordinary and derived adjunctions of [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations]. Put $E_{n,T}=D(\Delta_Te_{n,T})$. Write $P_f\dashv S_f$ for system inverse image and total derived direct image, and $G_{f,n}\dashv R_{f,n}^{\mathcal T}$ for the constant-$C_n$ tower adjunction. Exact localization of the inverse of the ordinary unit-normalized evaluation mate gives $b_{f,n}:E_{n,X}P_f\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f,n}E_{n,Y}$. The specified derived mate
$$d_{f,n}:E_{n,Y}S_f\longrightarrow R_{f,n}^{\mathcal T}E_{n,X}$$
of $b_{f,n}^{-1}$ is invertible. Under $E_n\cong D(\Delta)D(e_n)$ it is the pasted composite of the single-level evaluation direct-image mate $D(e_{n,Y})S_f\to Rf_{*,n}D(e_{n,X})$ and the unit-normalized diagonal mate $D(\Delta_Y)Rf_{*,n}\to R_{f,n}^{\mathcal T}D(\Delta_X)$. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, the inverse open-adjunction mate of $b_{j,n}$,
$$a_{j,n}:J_{j,n}^{\mathcal T}E_{n,U}\longrightarrow E_{n,X}J_j,$$
is invertible and factors similarly through the single-level open evaluation mate and the exact localization of the ordinary constant-diagram open comparison. The diagonal inverse open mate is $D(\operatorname{compConstIso}(j_!))^{-1}$ under the exact-composition identifications and the specified localized open adjunctions. All statements hold on whole unbounded derived categories before any evaluation of morphisms, with no coefficient flatness or boundedness assumption.

proof.text: Recover the ordinary single-level pullback comparison by evaluating the specified inverse tower mate at zero, exactly as in evaluationLevelPullOrdinary. A natural transformation between these constant towers has equal components: naturality for the unique map from any index to zero gives the equality after cancelling identities. Consequently the ordinary tower square is the paste of this single-level square and the identity-component constant-diagram square. This checks the chosen transformation itself and retains its unit normalization.

Apply the exact-square composition calculation of lem-pod-derived-exact-square-composition to the ordinary identity, with evaluation and the constant diagram as the two horizontal factors. Simplifying the exact-composition identifications gives evaluation_pull_pasting for the inverse of evalP. Cancel its invertible factors to obtain evaluation_pull_pasting_forward for evalP itself.

Use the existing evalR_isIso theorem for the specified direct-image mate and the existing chi_mate calculation of the canonical comparison from lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization. The latter identifies evaluationDiagonalDirect with chi for precisely the level and tower adjunctions in the statement. No new choice of direct-image comparison is made.

Apply Mathlib mateEquiv_vcomp to the inverse-image paste, transporting its top and bottom edges by evaluationDiagonal. Naturality and cancellation of those isomorphisms yield the direct-image factorization on each object; substitute chi_mate. These are components of an equality of derived natural transformations and do not test a morphism by evaluating it at tower indices.

For any exact ordinary adjunction whose right adjoint is also exact, compare the unit of its right-derived adjunction, transported through rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory, with the unit of exactLocalizationDerivedAdjunction. Localization extensionality reduces the equality to QK. The derived unit factorization, the right-derived comparison factorization, and the exact localized unit equation give the identical image of the ordinary unit. Adjunction.ext therefore identifies these adjunctions, retaining their specified units. Apply this to the single-level and tower open adjunctions.

The ordinary mate of the inverse constant-diagram restriction comparison is compConstIso for ordinary extension by zero, inverted: the constant-diagram mate calculation const_mate reduces it to the triangle identity. Apply lem-sf-exact-localization-inverse-mate and the adjunction identifications of the preceding step to get the stated exact-composition formula for evaluationDiagonalOpen.

Use the existing evalJInv_isIso theorem for open evaluation. Apply the bijective mate correspondence and mateEquiv_vcomp in reverse to evaluation_pull_pasting_forward; transport the two edges by evaluationDiagonal and cancel the inverse isomorphisms. This gives exactly the required open factorization. Combine it with the diagonal equation of the preceding step. All constructions are on whole unbounded derived categories with the original coefficient maps.

lean.statement: theorem semilinearEvaluationDerivedAdjunction (n : ℕ) : (∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y), IsIso (evalR C τ n f) ∧ evaluationDiagonalDirect C f n = (StrictTower.DiagonalNormalization.chi (C n) f).hom ∧ ∀ M : Derived C τ X, (evalR C τ n f).app M ≫ (StrictTower.R (C n) f).map ((evaluationDiagonal C τ n X).hom.app M) = (evaluationDiagonal C τ n Y).hom.app ((R C τ f).obj M) ≫ (StrictTower.DiagonalNormalization.delta (C n) Y).map ((evaluationLevelDirect C τ f n).app M) ≫ (StrictTower.DiagonalNormalization.chi (C n) f).hom.app ((VaryingRing.ev C τ X n).obj M)) ∧ (∀ {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j], IsIso (evalJInv C τ n j) ∧ (∀ M : Derived C τ U, (evalJInv C τ n j).app M ≫ (evaluationDiagonal C τ n X).hom.app ((J C τ j).obj M) = (StrictTower.J (C n) j).map ((evaluationDiagonal C τ n U).hom.app M) ≫ (evaluationDiagonalOpen C j n).app ((VaryingRing.ev C τ U n).obj M) ≫ (StrictTower.DiagonalNormalization.delta (C n) X).map ((evaluationLevelOpen C τ j n).app M)) ∧ evaluationDiagonalOpen C j n = (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : StrictTower.Modules (C n) U ⥤ StrictTower.Towers (C n) U) (StrictTower.towerJ (C n) j)).inv ≫ (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso (Functor.compConstIso ℕᵒᵖ (StrictTower.moduleJ (C n) j))).inv ≫ (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso (StrictTower.moduleJ (C n) j) (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ)).hom)
